# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

screens.why2: 'Setup, extra steps or learning' and 'up to four, each up to 9 words' are plain, and my two rows are in a super's own words.
screens.why3: I know what a super has to change: narrate short videos during the site walks instead of after, then check what Fresco wrote before it goes to the crew or Procore.
screens.why4: My two rows are distinct steps a super takes himself, one a new habit on the walk and one a check before sending, and 'Leave this out of the study' is the right escape for a founder who isn't sure.
screens.why5: Both rows are what I typed, word for word, and the belief takes the first one without changing what it means.
screens.why7: Each row is one effort under 9 words, in base form, taken by the super himself (not a sign-off, not Procore fit, not the purchase), and 'talk over videos on walks' is a real habit change that some would refuse, so the belief can hold or fail; the founder-side escape is there.
screens.instead: Same screen, with the belief reading 'Most would take short videos and talk over them on their site walks.' so it uses the trade's word for the walk.

screens.why1: Right after I typed what supers have to do to start, Keel shows my steps back as rows to check, which is the natural next beat; the title is repeated in the intro but that is cosmetic.
screens.why2: 'Take short videos and talk over them on walks' and 'check and fix the notes before they go out' are how I'd say it to a super, with no word from outside the trailer.
screens.why3: Both are things a superintendent does with their own hands on their own walk and in their own trailer, so any super can say whether they'd do them.
screens.why4: Two distinct efforts, the new on-site habit and the review before the notes reach the crew or Procore; neither repeats the other and neither is Compatibility's or Purchase friction's ground.
screens.why5: The first row is my mechanism, 'short videos with voiceover', in plainer words, and the second is the honest catch my sceptics raised; dropping 'or upload photos' still leaves the step I actually want to test.
screens.why7: Each row is one base-form effort the super takes themselves, in the third person, under 9 words, with no other role's sign-off; the belief 'Most would take short videos and talk over them on walks' can be met by a Yes or an 'Only if it doesn't slow the walk', and refuted by a Probably not or a No.

screens.why1: Right after I listed and checked what supers have to do to start, it's obvious why I'm now asked which effort is the real hurdle to test.
screens.why2: Short videos, talking over them, site walks, notes going out: that's how supers and I talk about the job, and I can read it at once.
screens.why3: I know from my own users whether a super will narrate on a walk and whether they'll review notes before texting the crew, so I can answer from what I've seen.
screens.why4: Both rows are mine, two distinct efforts the super takes themselves (a habit on the walk, a check before sending), and neither repeats Procore fit or getting it bought.
screens.why5: The picked row and the belief are my words as typed: narrated short videos on site walks, nothing reworded.
screens.why7: Both options measure one thing, an effort the super takes themselves, in their voice, at most 9 words each and within the 1 to 4; the belief is a single effort a stranger can say yes, only-if or no to, so it can hold or fail against the 1-in-3 bar.

screens.why1: Asking just before the study goes out whether to collect emails from people who say yes fits here, and I sell per site, so I want a list of supers and contractors willing to try it on a live job.
screens.why2: Offer a pilot, Yes or No, with a hint that shows the exact line respondents will see, reads in one pass.
screens.why3: Whether I want trial sign-ups from this study is my own call, and I can make it.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers the choice, and the two options are distinct.
screens.why5: My plan's "pilot" is a paid pilot on one site that the contractor signs off on, but here it means a stranger leaving an email, so the word has drifted a little from what I meant.
screens.instead: Ask people who say yes if they'd try it on one of their jobs? (Yes, ask them for an email / No) -- the GC decides on a paid site pilot later.

screens.why1: Picking who asks the questions belongs in the last step before the link goes out, after the questions and the pilot offer are settled.
screens.why2: It is clear enough, but the hint packs four things into one block (video, typing instead, the preselect, 400 credits, text message), and it says 'tap Saskia to hear her' when both rows have a play button, so I read it twice.
screens.why3: I know my supers, guys in a trailer at the end of the day, so I can judge which voice they would stay on the line with.
screens.why4: Two named voices with a 5-second clip are distinct, but the interviewer is on video and I only get to hear them, not see the face I am locking and paying 400 credits for.
screens.why5: It names my people as construction superintendents and says the link goes by text, which is how my crews actually get things; nothing of mine is changed.
screens.instead: Who should ask construction superintendents your questions? Pick one; you can watch each for 5 s. Daphne (picked for you) ▶ Watch · Saskia ▶ Watch. Hint: The interviewer asks each question aloud on video and shows it on screen, so supers can tap or type instead. The voice and face you pick are recorded once for this project for 400 credits.

screens.why1: After choosing who asks the questions, deciding how supers will answer the link is the natural last step before sending.
screens.why2: Short, plain choices; 'AI interviewer · Daphne' is explained in the line under it, so I get it on first read.
screens.why3: I know my supers -- in the trailer at end of day, phone in hand, mostly tapping and texting -- so I can pick for them.
screens.why4: AI video, read-and-tap, or let them choose covers it, the three are distinct, and the descriptions say what each means for the super.
screens.why5: Nothing here changes what I typed; it only says how construction superintendents get the questions.

screens.why1: After choosing how superintendents answer, deciding who gets a link is the obvious last step before sending the study.
screens.why2: The three choices read plainly on first pass; 'Contacts page' and 'signs in with Google' are clear enough to a founder using the tool.
screens.why3: I know whether I'm sending to supers I know by name from our pilots and intros or posting in a group, so this is answerable from my own situation.
screens.why4: Named people, a Keel-found list, and an open group link are distinct and cover how I'd reach supers; no escape is needed for a founder's own sending choice.
screens.why5: Nothing of my product or roles is changed here; it is purely about distribution, and my pick 'People I know by name' is kept.

screens.why_b1: The verdict *Too few to call* sits on every card with *4 counted · 5 needed to call it* beside it, so I know nothing is decided because I'm one counted person short; but the line under the title oddly names only Compatibility when all three are in the same state.
screens.why_b2: There is no chart on the stage page, but the tally reads at a glance: 3 beliefs, all 3 too few to call, 7 answered, 4 counted, 5 needed.
screens.why_b3: Compatibility, Relative advantage and Adoption friction carry my beliefs as I checked them (talking over the site noise, hours back plus same-day action items, short videos on walks).
screens.why_b4: *5 needed to call it* implies I need more answers, but the screen never says to send the study to more superintendents or why 3 of the 7 weren't counted, so I'm left to work out the next step myself.
screens.why_b5: It claims nothing: n is shown (7 answered, 4 counted), the low count is said outright, and nothing is called held or failed; only the garbled statement (*sends the notes... and gets back the notes...*) reads sloppily.
screens.instead: All three solution beliefs are too few to call: 4 of the 7 who answered counted (3 weren't, because ...), and 5 are needed, so get at least one more superintendent through the study before reading anything into the solution.

screens.why_b1: The status word *Too few to call* sits right beside *4 counted · 5 needed to call it*, so I know there is no verdict yet and exactly why.
screens.why_b2: The bars and their for/against labels read straight off, but the strip's *your bar · 4 of 5* next to *no more than 1 in 3* took me a second look: I could not tell at first whether 4 of 5 is the bar, the count or the floor.
screens.why_b3: The card is Compatibility and the belief is word for word the one I checked: *Most construction superintendents could talk over the noise on site.*
screens.why_b4: *Ray's no is the one to ask about* gives me a person to call, but the screen never says that one more answer decides it: a yes holds at 4 of 5, a no fails at 3 of 5.
screens.why_b5: The count is honest (a small group, a lean, not a call), but the question asked about my *last daily log*, which I write in the trailer, not on the noisy walk, so Ray's No may be about the wrong moment, and the unattributed crane quote has nothing to do with talking over noise.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of 4 counted could talk over the noise, so one more answer settles it (a yes holds, a no fails); ask Ray what was loud on his last site walk, and ask about the walk, not the log in the trailer.

screens.why_b1: The verdict, Too few to call, sits right beside its deciding number: 4 counted, 5 needed to call it.
screens.why_b2: Better 3 and Same 1 of 4 read fast, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' with the marker at 4 mixes up the 5-person floor with my 1-in-3 bar, and 'Same' quietly holds 'worse' too, so I had to look twice.
screens.why_b3: The card is Relative advantage with my belief word for word, hours back and action items to the crew the same day, though the bar line names only 'hours back', the half Keel said it would test.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't say that one more counted super's answer would call it, or that 3 of 4 saying a lot better is a good lean on my benefit.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible (5 answered, 4 counted, Luis's guess left out), the small group is named a lean rather than a call, and nothing is claimed as held.
screens.instead: So far 3 of 4 supers say a lot better and 1 (Denise, who finishes her log on the tablet before she leaves) says no difference, inside your 1-in-3 limit; one more counted answer calls it, so send it to another super whose log still waits until the trailer.

screens.why_b1: The status *Too few to call* sits right beside its deciding numbers, *4 counted · 5 needed*, so I know there is no verdict yet and exactly why.
screens.why_b2: The bars plainly count answers per option, but the strip's *your bar · 4 of 5* with its marker at 4 and a ghost cell takes a second look: it is unclear whether 4 is people needed for, the floor, or the bar itself.
screens.why_b3: *Adoption friction* and *Most would take short videos and talk over them on walks.* are the dimension and belief I checked, word for word, though the bar line *You said take short videos...* is an odd fragment.
screens.why_b4: *Nothing is settled here yet* is generic: it does not say one more counted superintendent would decide it, or that two of my three yeses hang on not slowing the walk, which is a design point for capture during the walk.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible, Luis's guess is set apart, the condition split is shown, and the line says outright that a small group gives a lean, not a call.
screens.instead: Too few to call: one more counted answer decides it -- so far 3 of 4 would do it, but 2 only if it doesn't slow the site walk, so make the video take seconds, not minutes.

screens.why_b1: Each box opens on its verdict, Too few to call, with the deciding number right under it (4 counted · 5 needed to call it), so I know neither line was decided and why.
screens.why_b3: Compatibility's line is the talk-over-the-noise belief I checked, and Relative advantage shows the full line I signed off on; it is the hours-back-plus-action-items version rather than the narrower hours-back line Keel actually tested, but it is mine.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed to call it' implies I need one more counted answer per line, but the screen never says to send to more supers, and it does not say what Denise's done-before-the-gate or Ray's log-can-wait mean for the scribe pitch.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible on every box (4 counted, 1 against, 1 asked), the low count is named as too few to call, and one quote each is shown as one person, not a theme.
screens.why_b6: Neither quote is anything I typed: Denise finishes her log on a tablet before the gate and says schedule and no-show subs eat her day, and Ray says the log waits till morning when the crane's down; both suggest the log is not the worst hour of a super's day, which cuts against my 'hours back' benefit.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 of 5 counted on each line, so send to at least one more super before reading these; the one 'against' on each says the daily log isn't what eats the day (schedule and subs are), which is a warning for the hours-back pitch, not a verdict yet.

screens.why1: As the first screen it plainly checks that I'm on a Procore or ACC job, which is who the study wants, so it's obvious why it comes first.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are the platforms my jobs live on, so I get it on first read, though the doubled 'run ... run on' is a little clumsy.
screens.why3: I know exactly which platform each of my jobs is set up on.
screens.why4: Yes and No covers it on a gate, and there's correctly no escape chip on a screener.
screens.why5: It names the segment's tools, which are my own everyday words, and nothing of the founder's product or plan reaches me.
screens.why6: Short, one question, two options anyone can hold, and 'ACC' is said as letters on site anyway, though §17 has a screener close on a plain 'Yes or no.' rather than 'I'll read 2 options.'
screens.instead: Are any of the jobs you're running now on Procore or ACC? Yes or no.

screens.why1: Right after confirming my jobs run on Procore, asking whether my daily log ran past the day is the obvious first question about the record I keep.
screens.why2: Daily log, jobsite, the last 5 working days: those are my words, and I can answer on one hearing.
screens.why3: I know exactly whether I was finishing the log at home or in the truck this week.
screens.why4: Yes and No are complete and distinct for this, and the chips belong to the story box after a Yes, not to the gate.
screens.why5: Nothing of the product leaks to me, but 'after leaving the jobsite' narrows the founder's problem of typing up the log after the walks: a super who types it up in the trailer has the problem and still has to say No.
screens.why6: It is one short question with 'Yes or no.', easy to hold and answer on one hearing.
screens.why7: It is on the one measure with the fixed Yes and No in order, no escape, and both answers are true of someone, so the belief can be supported or refuted; but the gate drifts from the founder's problem by adding 'after leaving the jobsite', so the share undercounts and one rule is bent.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you type up the daily log after your site walks? Yes · No.

screens.why1: Part 2 has just started, and after being asked whether I finished my daily log after leaving the site, showing me the idea now makes obvious sense.
screens.why2: Site walk, action items, assignees, Procore and ACC are all my words, but 'AI scribe' is not something anyone on a job site says; I'd call it an app that writes up my notes.
screens.why3: I walk the site, take photos, assign items to subs and push stuff into Procore every day, so I can picture this on my own job.
screens.why4: A card to read with no options.
screens.why5: Nothing leaks that shouldn't, since the card is shown on purpose, but the belief line only repeats what the thing does ('turn your videos into notes') instead of what it would change for me, like the hours spent uploading and finishing the daily log at night.
screens.why6: It says cleanly with no slashes or brackets, but 'the scribe' three times plus a closing belief that repeats the opening line makes a long, circular listen.
screens.instead: Imagine Fresco, an app that turns your site walk videos into notes. On your walk you take short videos and talk over them; it writes the notes with photos, who's on it and due dates, texts the crew their items, and sends it all to Procore or ACC in one click. The people building it believe it would get your daily log done before you leave the site.

screens.why1: Right after the idea card, it makes sense to ask whether I could even talk on site the way this thing needs, since that is the first thing it depends on.
screens.why2: The words are mine, but 'talk over the noise' doesn't say talk to whom or into what, so I'd read it twice to work out that it means narrating into my phone.
screens.why3: My last daily log was typed up in the trailer after the walk, so pinning it to the log instead of the walk makes me guess which part of the day it means.
screens.why4: Yes easily, most of the time, only sometimes and no cover how loud my sites get, with no overlap, and I can't tell fits as the out.
screens.why5: The card names it as an AI scribe for site walk videos, which is shown on purpose, and nothing else of the founder's plan or terms leaks into the question.
screens.why6: It is short and one question, with four short options and the escape said last, easy to hold after one hearing.
screens.why7: It is an ability with the four fixed rungs in order and I can't tell apart, so it can hold or fail, but the occasion is the daily log rather than the site walk and 'into your phone' is dropped, which bends the condition the card's good example tests.
screens.instead: Think of your last site walk. Could you have spoken into your phone over the noise? Yes, easily / Yes, most of the time / Only sometimes / No, or I can't tell.

screens.why1: Right after the idea card and the noise question, asking whether Fresco would have done my last log better is the obvious next thing.
screens.why2: I'd say 'my last daily log'; the add-on 'when you had to keep an accurate record of the day's work' is stiff and makes me read it twice, since every daily log is that.
screens.why3: I write a daily log every day and know how the last one went, so I can judge whether something from my walk videos would have helped.
screens.why4: A lot better, a little better, no difference, worse, plus I can't tell covers every answer I'd give, with no overlap.
screens.why5: Fresco and what it is come from the idea card shown on purpose, and the question names none of its benefits or anyone's plan.
screens.why6: The options and escape say well as a short list, but the stem runs past twenty words with a trailing clause that's a mouthful when heard once.
screens.why7: The four fixed rungs in order, two for and two against, and I can't tell apart all meet the card, but the occasion is any last log rather than the hard one where the record was at stake, like the log I finished after leaving site.
screens.instead: Think of the last daily log you had to finish after you left the site. Would Fresco have made that one better for you, or not? A lot better · A little better · No difference · Worse · I can't tell

screens.why1: Right after hearing what Fresco is and whether it would do my log better, it's obvious to ask whether I'd actually shoot video and talk through my walk to feed it.
screens.why2: Short videos and talking over them on a site walk are plain to me; I can answer on first hearing.
screens.why3: I walk my site every day with my phone out for photos, so I know whether I'd narrate video instead.
screens.why4: Yes, a real catch (it can't slow my walk), probably not and no are distinct, and I can't tell fits as the escape.
screens.why5: The card is shown on purpose and the step is said in my terms, so nothing leaks beyond the idea I was shown.
screens.why6: One short question, four short options read as a list with the condition switched to your, and one escape said last.
screens.why7: The effort is one I'd take myself, the four answers are in the card's order with a condition specific to my work (the walk's pace, not true of every step), two count for and two against, and I can't tell sits apart.
